Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you reported at
an intersection in Houston, Texas. Before we begin, do you consent to this call being recorded?
A: Yes, that's fine.
Q: Please state your full address for the file.
A: I'd rather just give the city and zip for now. I live in Houston.
Q: That works for the moment. Can you walk me through what happened at the intersection?
A: I was driving through on a green light, heading straight. A pickup coming from the cross street didn't stop and hit
the driver's side of my car as I was crossing.
Q: Did you see the pickup before the impact?
A: Only a second before. I saw it coming but there wasn't time to do anything.
Q: Were there any witnesses, or a police report?
A: An officer came out and filled out a report. I think there was a man in a car behind the pickup who stopped and
talked to him.
Q: Where were you taken after the collision?
A: An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They X-rayed my shoulder and my neck.
Q: Can you describe the injury you're claiming?
A: My right shoulder hurts badly when I raise my arm. The doctor said it could be a strain or possibly a tear, and I've
been referred for an MRI. I'm also stiff in the neck, but the shoulder is the main problem.
Q: Have you seen a doctor since then?
A: Yes, I've been going to a physical therapist twice a week. I can't lift anything heavy at work right now.
Q: Is there anything you'd like to add about the accident?
A: Just that I was following the rules that day. I hope the other driver's insurance takes responsibility.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
